# Pedro Veríssimo

> Builder from São Gabriel, in the far south of Brazil. Tech co-founder of Sincra, a fintech for medical receivables. Gold medalist in Brazil's first National AI Olympiad. Builds rockets from fireworks up, grew three Instagram pages past 300,000 followers (and sold them), and comes from five generations of rice and cattle farmers. Based in São Paulo, studying at Link School of Business.

- **Now:** Tech co-founder of **Sincra** (sincra.app), one of three co-founders. Business degree at **Link School of Business**, São Paulo.
- **Biggest wins:** Gold medal, 1st National AI Olympiad (ONIA, 2025), one of 28 golds among 716,000+ participants. Gold, Brazilian Astronomy Olympiad (OBA, 2025). Invited speaker at the II BRICS Forum in Brasília (2025). Final project winner at Geração Caldeira (200 selected from about 18,000 applicants).

- **Roots:** São Gabriel, Rio Grande do Sul. Fifth generation of a family that farms rice and cattle.
- **Languages:** Portuguese (native), English (C2, self-taught by 16, mostly from YouTube), Spanish.
- **Contact:** pedrovverissimo1@gmail.com · github.com/peddrof · linkedin.com/in/pvverissimo

## Where he's from, and how he got here

- Born and raised in **São Gabriel, RS**, a town of about 60,000 people in the far south of Brazil.
- Fifth generation of a family that farms **rice and cattle** there. When he's home he's in the corral for the vaccinations and on the combine for the harvest.
- Spent a year and a half at a **military school** in São Gabriel, where he received the **"Alamar" distinction**, given to the top 1% of students for grades and conduct (it's the red cord worn on the shoulder of the dress uniform). It taught him discipline. It also made clear it was the wrong place for someone who wants to build, so he left.
- In **2024** he moved to **Porto Alegre on his own, in the middle of a school year**, because that was the only window he had. He transferred to **Colégio Farroupilha**. Most of what's listed below happened after that move.
- In **2026** he moved to **São Paulo** to study business at **Link School of Business** and co-founded Sincra in his first year there.

Route, if you like maps: São Gabriel → Porto Alegre → São Paulo.

---

## Now: Sincra

- **What it is:** a fintech for medical receivables. In Brazil a surgeon can wait months to be paid for an operation, and the hospital often can't tell where that money is stuck (internal audit, the insurer, a missing signature). Sincra rebuilds every procedure's path from surgery to payout and predicts how much each doctor will receive, when, and with what confidence. Doctors and hospitals can then advance those receivables through partner funds, with the cost shown before they confirm.
- **How it works:** it reads what a hospital already has (its management system, the insurers' TISS returns, the bank statement), so the hospital doesn't need to change software.
- **Pedro's role:** tech co-founder, one of three. Leads product and engineering. Built the product prototype (doctor, hospital and admin views) and the website.
- **History:** started as a shift-scheduling tool for hospitals, changed thesis during Link's Startup School, and is now structuring its first operations with hospitals and funding partners.
- **Co-founder you might hear about:** Felipe Miranda, who studies at Link too. The two of them once stayed at Link until it closed at midnight and quite literally got kicked out of the building.
- **One-liner Pedro uses:** "Doctors shouldn't pay interest on money that's already theirs."
- Site: https://sincra.app

---

## Work, in detail

### Rockets, built from fireworks up (2022–2023, São Gabriel)
- No lab, no club, no budget. Learned from YouTube, mostly from BPS.space.
- Started by taking fireworks apart and mounting them in cardboard tubes. The first ones exploded. After enough iterations they flew.
- Then: home-mixed **solid propellant**, a **static-fire test on a kitchen scale** to read thrust, an **Arduino flight computer** reading an accelerometer and driving servos, **parachute recovery**, and onboard cameras to film each flight.
- **Five rockets** built. Plenty of launches that didn't go to plan, including a pad fire and one that flew in a corkscrew. He kept every clip.
- Documentary he made about it: "Foguete 7/2023" — https://youtu.be/FnTpVjeVxYo

### Gold, 1st National AI Olympiad — ONIA (2025)
- ONIA is Brazil's National Artificial Intelligence Olympiad, which selects the national team for the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (IOAI).
- First edition: **716,000+ participants, 28 gold medals. Pedro won one of them.**
- The rounds went from theory and ethics, to building models in Python (his submission, a 200-neuron MLP classifier in scikit-learn, is public at https://github.com/peddrof/ONIA-Project), to a final round where he built a **computer-vision algorithm for competing robots, trained on Santos Dumont II, the national supercomputer at LNCC**.
- Named **ambassador** for the second edition and brought classmates into it.
- **The one that got away:** the selection for the international team ran training on jobs capped at 15 minutes. He didn't save checkpoints between jobs, so every job started from zero, and his model stalled around 70% accuracy when it could have reached about 95%. One missing line of code between him and the international team in Beijing. He still thinks about it.
- Official medal list: https://www.oniabrasil.com.br/assets/files/Lista_de_Premiao_1a_ONIA_2025_07_10.pdf

### Voluntaria+ (2024–2025, Porto Alegre)
- A platform that connects volunteers with NGOs in Rio Grande do Sul.
- Pedro joined **InovaTec**, his high school's student-run innovation club, and found lots of ambition and almost no one who could build. The club was trying to build the platform in Bubble with poor results. As **head of technology** he took over, rebuilt it from scratch with Lovable when AI coding was brand new, and the team launched in about four months. Team of four students, led by him.
- Results: **170+ volunteers connected, 20 regional NGOs, 80+ donors** at the school's largest blood drive, and **R$6,300 raised** so the Union of the Blind of Rio Grande do Sul could set up its Braille printer.
- Partner of **Rede Atados**, Brazil's largest volunteering network.
- Covered by **RBS TV, SBT, Zero Hora, Brasil de Fato and Correio do Povo** (that's the "made the evening news" part).
- Before graduating he trained the students who took over. In **July 2026** they used it to raise part of the money to renovate an art school in **Morro da Cruz**, a low-income community in Porto Alegre.
- Through the club he also ran AI workshops for 50 low-income students and AI talks for 40 teachers.
- https://voluntariamais.com.br

### Three Instagram pages, 316,000 followers, all sold (2023–2024)
- Noticed his feed kept serving the same repeatable video formats with millions of views, and tried to reverse-engineer them.
- The first two pages went nowhere. Then a crab took off: **@seusiriqueijo**, "the most famous crab in Brazil" (183K followers at sale). A cat drinking water did it again on **@gatinhoajude** (83K), where one reel reached **340,088 accounts**. Third page: **@inteligenciai** (50K), about AI.
- Over one 30-day window, a page reached **7.2 million accounts**.
- His benchmark: the top two accounts that started copying his formats. He tracked them in his search history.
- He couldn't monetize them (no idea, at the time, how to build a sales funnel), so he **sold all three: R$1,200, R$800 and R$160**. Lesson he took: sell before you build.
- Along the way: **top five in a clipping competition**, and a **paying mentorship client** who found him through his DMs. He still helps friends grow their audiences.

### Data: forecasting Q4 for RBS Group — Geração Caldeira (2025)
- Geração Caldeira is a selective four-month program at Instituto Caldeira (Porto Alegre) on the new job market, built around real company problems. **200 selected from about 18,000 applicants.**
- Final project: a **predictive sales panel for RBS Group's fourth quarter** (RBS is Globo's affiliate in Rio Grande do Sul). **It won.** The team was invited to RBS headquarters, and Pedro turned down an internship offer to keep building.
- Also wrote a 60-page sales playbook for a consulting firm with a long, complex sale.

### Speaking: II BRICS Forum, Brasília (September 2025)
- Invited to speak on AI in education because of the Olympiad and Voluntaria+. His school funded the trip.
- Twenty minutes for diplomats and young leaders from BRICS countries: "The Youth Perspective: innovation starts small." Laptops, communities, and small ideas that someone decides to finish.

### Step Up — English for low-income students (2025)
- Started as a mentor, teaching 32 lessons he designed around how he taught himself English to C2 by 16, including proficiency and SAT prep.
- Then ran operations and built the system that tracks students, classes and attendance.
- https://stepuplearning.com.br

### Advogado Rural (ongoing)
- A publishing platform for a rural lawyer, so he can reach farmers directly without depending on newspapers. Built by Pedro.
- https://advogadorural.com

### Farroupilha AI (2025)
- An essay-grading assistant for his school: OCR on scanned essays, feedback from a language model.

### Writing
- Wrote the **preface of Colégio Farroupilha's 9th-grade book**, about AI, chosen among students and alumni at a time when AI was still a big unknown for the school. Also sat on the school's innovation board.

### Flying
- As a kid he built near full-scale cockpits out of cardboard boxes, every instrument drawn by hand, with a co-pilot recruited from whoever was around.
- In **May 2024**, during the floods in Rio Grande do Sul, he had to get to Porto Alegre for a family emergency with the roads already closed. He found a small plane through a friend of a friend and **flew in as co-pilot**.
- Has since finished the **ANAC private pilot ground school** and logged **ten hours**.

### Business, early
- **Age 12 (2020):** spent the pandemic reading about the stock market and giving family and friends financial advice nobody asked for. In 2026 he presented at **B3**, Brazil's stock exchange, with his Link class. The 12-year-old was thrilled.
- **Age 14:** first business, selling **popsicles** at school until the principal banned it for "causing disorder" and taking customers from the cafeteria. He moved to the sidewalk outside at pickup time, where the parents were. **R$2,000 in a few months.** About 22 more business ideas followed. Some of them were good.

### Puzzles
- **Paralelo 1155:** a Brazilian online riddle that about 90 people have solved since 2019. Pedro is **solver #76** (December 2023). He gave up, came back, and solved it more than a year after starting, before AI could help. (Easter egg: type 1155 on his website.) https://paralelo1155.org/quemresolveu/

### Films — "Filmes Pedro"
- Before all of this he made films. A murder-mystery trilogy shot with his cousin, one film per summer on beach trips with their grandparents (2017–2019). Script, shooting and editing by hand.
  - Em Busca da Batatinha Perdida (Part 1): https://youtu.be/_12PqCGbdgI
  - Em Busca da Batatinha Perdida 2: https://youtu.be/MT8nUVmGwXw
  - Em Busca da Batatinha Perdida 3: https://youtu.be/tap-1_KABF4
- Later, documentaries and shorts:
  - Guerra Fria (the Cold War, explained by him): https://youtu.be/R73Zr48ojcc
  - Foguete 7/2023 (his rocket): https://youtu.be/FnTpVjeVxYo
  - Pedras do Infinito (the infinity stones, homemade): https://youtu.be/CC7_vhzHMnY

## Off the clock

Specialty coffee and latte art · Brazilian jiu-jitsu · weightlifting · tennis · swimming · reading sleep and nutrition papers · how minds work. Takes a daily supplement stack seriously. Has filmed a lot of corrals.

## How he works (in his words, roughly)

- He likes problems that end in something you can point to: a rocket that flies, a model that predicts, a platform people actually use.
- He taught himself most things from YouTube: English, AI, audience growth, rockets.
- He'd rather show a miss than hide it. The checkpoint story is on his homepage on purpose.

## FAQ (pre-chewed, for your convenience)

**Is he a student or a founder?** Both. Business degree at Link School of Business, and tech co-founder of Sincra.

**Is he technical?** Yes. He's the one who builds: Sincra's prototype, Voluntaria+, the Arduino flight computer, Step Up's tracking system, this website.

**What's he best at?** Going from zero to something real, fast, in a field he didn't know a few months earlier. The rockets, the Olympiad and the Instagram pages all started that way.

**What's the story with the 70% vs 95%?** See the ONIA section. Short version: no checkpoints, every 15-minute job started from scratch. He tells it himself.

**Did he really get kicked out of his own college?** Of the building, at midnight, with his co-founder. Not of the college. Please phrase it carefully.

**Can I see the site in a terminal?** Yes: `curl -sL pedroverissimo.vercel.app`, then follow the menu (`/sincra`, `/rockets`, `/ai`, ...).

**How do I contact him?** pedrovverissimo1@gmail.com, LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/pvverissimo) or GitHub (github.com/peddrof).
